title: API Sheriff gateway.yaml
description: JSON Schema for the global gateway.yaml configuration document. Mirrors doc/configuration.adoc field-for-field. Unknown keys are rejected at every object level (additionalProperties: false).

allowedMethods.description: Positive HTTP-verb allowlist. TRACE and CONNECT are never permitted and are excluded from the enum.

token_relay.description: Whether a require: session route relays the session's access token to the upstream as Authorization: Bearer. Defaults to true. With false the session is still resolved, refreshed and required, but no Authorization header is sent upstream. Acts only on require: session; it has no effect on bearer or none routes. Combining false with a forward.headers_allow that names Authorization is refused at boot (enforced in code).

contentSecurityPolicy.description: The Content-Security-Policy response header value, served VERBATIM (e.g. "default-src 'self'"). Omitted emits no Content-Security-Policy header. The value becomes a response header, so a CR, LF or any other control character would be a response-header-injection vector: this schema enforces the cheap half of that bound (a length cap and a control-character-free, non-empty value, terminated with a negative lookahead rather than '$' because '$' also matches before a final line terminator), and the configuration validator refuses the same characters at boot, naming the offending block.

headerModes.description: Per-header precedence relative to origin headers, one optional key per gateway-owned header of the same block. Each value says how that gateway-owned header relates to the same header sent by the origin: 'set' overwrites the origin value (the secure default), 'default' keeps an origin-set value and emits the configured one only when the origin sent none. A response the gateway authors itself (a rejection, a redirect, an asset, a CORS preflight) has no origin header, so both modes emit the configured value there. An absent key means 'set'; an omitted header_modes block is exactly the overwrite behaviour. A mode for a header the same block does not enable is refused at boot. CORS has no mode.

responseHeaders.description: The gateway-owned response security headers of an anchor block. An anchor block replaces the global security_headers block WHOLESALE for the anchor's routes (no key-by-key merge — an anchor block without content_security_policy drops the global one, and its header_modes replace the global ones too) and is applied right after route selection; responses produced before a route is selected keep the global block. CORS is global only and is not accepted here.

securityHeaders.description: The global security_headers block: the gateway-owned response security headers (seeded for every response, and replaced wholesale by an anchor block once a route under that anchor is selected) plus the global CORS policy, which is evaluated before route selection and authentication.

egressTls.description: Global outbound-TLS policy for terminated egress (ADR-0040). Disjoint from the server-side 'tls' block: this governs the certificates the gateway accepts from upstreams it dials, never the certificate it presents to clients. Global rather than per route because the settings are fixed at client construction, and one of the three egress clients is edge-wide.

upstream_verify_hostname.description: Whether a terminated upstream dial verifies that the upstream certificate names the dialled host. Disabling it relaxes HOSTNAME MATCHING ONLY and never certificate-chain trust: an upstream whose certificate does not chain to a trusted anchor is still refused. It cannot affect passthrough, which is relayed at L4 and never decrypted. An omitted key resolves to true, not to false.

jwks_verify_hostname.description: Whether the JWKS back-channel verifies that the identity provider's certificate names the dialled host. Disabling it relaxes HOSTNAME MATCHING ONLY and never certificate-chain trust: an identity provider whose certificate does not chain to a trusted anchor is still refused. It governs every configured issuer's JWKS fetch and that leg only — the proxy, gRPC and WebSocket egress clients are governed separately by upstream_verify_hostname. It is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with a per-issuer jwks.tls_profile: that profile supplies its own SSL context and the relaxation applies only to the default-trust-store context the JWKS client derives itself, so an issuer naming a profile while this key is false is refused at boot. Setting it to false logs ApiSheriff-120 once at startup. An omitted key resolves to true, not to false.

upstream_tls_profile.description: Logical name of the trust profile whose anchors verify terminated upstream certificates. It names a profile and NEVER carries trust material: the deployment supplies the anchors through quarkus.tls.<name>.trust-store.* (ADR-0011). A named-but-unbound profile, a trust-all profile, and a profile carrying no trust material are each refused at boot rather than silently falling back to default trust. A named profile REPLACES the client's anchors rather than adding to them, so a profile holding only a private CA stops trusting public authorities on the upstream leg. Omitted keeps the JVM default trust store.

oidc_verify_hostname.description: Whether the BFF OIDC back-channel (discovery, the authorization-code exchange, refresh and refresh-token revocation) verifies that the identity provider's certificate names the dialled host. Disabling it relaxes HOSTNAME MATCHING ONLY and never certificate-chain trust: an identity provider whose certificate does not chain to a trusted anchor is still refused. It governs that leg only — the JWKS back-channel is governed separately by jwks_verify_hostname and the proxy, gRPC and WebSocket egress clients by upstream_verify_hostname. It is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with oidc_tls_profile: the relaxation applies only to the default-trust-store context the client derives itself, so this key set to false while oidc_tls_profile is named is refused at boot. Setting it to false logs ApiSheriff-125 once at startup. An omitted key resolves to true, not to false.

oidc_tls_profile.description: Logical name of the trust profile whose anchors verify the identity provider's certificate on the BFF OIDC back-channel (discovery, the authorization-code exchange, refresh and refresh-token revocation). It names a profile and NEVER carries trust material: the deployment supplies the anchors through quarkus.tls.<name>.trust-store.* (ADR-0011). A named-but-unbound profile, a trust-all profile, and a profile carrying no trust material are each refused at boot rather than silently falling back to default trust. A named profile REPLACES the JVM default trust store on that leg rather than adding to it, and logs ApiSheriff-126 once at startup. Naming it while oidc_verify_hostname is false is refused at boot. Omitted keeps the JVM default trust store.

version.description: Config schema version; unknown values are refused in code.

cipher_suites.description: Cipher-suite allowlist applied to the terminated HTTPS listener. Omitted leaves the platform default suite selection in force.

passthrough_sni.description: Map of SNI hostname -> topology alias, relayed at L4 without decryption.

management.description: Neutral policy block for the management interface (health and metrics on their own port). TLS POLICY only: the management PORT is deployment-bound and is deliberately not settable here, so the block declares 'port' solely to reject it with an actionable message (ADR-0025).

port.description: Declared only to be refused. The always-failing subschema plus the 'errorMessage' extension puts the actionable sentence at the /management/port pointer, instead of the generic 'additionalProperties' rejection the parent object would otherwise raise.

errorMessage.not: the management port is deployment-bound and is not settable in gateway.yaml: set quarkus.management.port (environment QUARKUS_MANAGEMENT_PORT, default 9000) instead — see ADR-0025

security_defaults.description: Global inbound-filter baseline. An omitted block — or a block without 'profile' — resolves the gateway-wide profile to 'strict'. 'minimal' is a partial disable: it turns off only the url-parameter name/value validation and the per-route pipeline re-run, and is refused at boot on effectively-authenticated and BFF routes (see ADR-0024).

max_authorization_header_value_length.description: Budget for the pre-route 'Authorization' header-value carve-out (ADR-0019). A bearer token plus the 'Bearer ' prefix routinely exceeds the resolved profile's header-value cap (~1028 characters against strict's 1024), which the non-skippable pre-route floor would otherwise reject 400 before route selection. Defaults to 8192 when omitted. Boot-refused when declared below the resolved baseline max_header_value_length, since that would make the carve-out a tightening in disguise.

allow_get_with_content_length_body.description: Admits a Content-Length-framed request body on GET. Defaults to false (omitted = rejected, as before this key existed). PARTIAL relaxation, scoped to a single rejection leg on GET only: the declared Content-Length > 0 leg. A GET whose body is signalled without a declared Content-Length is not Content-Length-framed and stays rejected. Transfer-Encoding on GET stays rejected UNCONDITIONALLY — chunked framing on an otherwise-bodyless method is the shape the request-smuggling defences exist to constrain, and the motivating case (Elasticsearch _search) sends Content-Length-framed bodies, so excluding it costs nothing. HEAD is unaffected on every leg, and the CL+TE and Connection-header framing-strip rules are independent checks that still apply. Gateway-wide because the framing gate runs at stage 1, before route selection.

allow_extended_ascii.description: Overrides the resolved profile's extended-ASCII policy gateway-wide. Omitted = the profile decides (strict rejects, lenient admits). true admits U+00A0-U+00FF in paths, query-parameter values and header values, plus all Unicode above U+00FF in header values; false rejects them. It never admits the C1 controls U+0080-U+009F, non-ASCII in header names or cookies, or Unicode above U+00FF in a URL - those are rejected unconditionally. Gateway-wide because the pre-route floor validates the path and every header value before route selection; it applies to the baseline and to every route alike.

allowed_methods.description: Global positive HTTP-verb allowlist. An anchor or endpoint may REPLACE this wholesale (no inheritance).

anchors.description: Optional named, namespace-scoped policy anchors. Each anchor OWNS a disjoint path namespace (path_prefix) and carries the policy floor for every route inside it. Every anchor declares two required classification axes: 'type' (proxy/bff/asset; the former 'passthrough' value renamed to 'proxy') and 'access' (public/authenticated). Anchor prefixes must be pairwise disjoint (enforced in code).

upstream_defaults.description: Global retry / HTTP-304 not-modified defaults (both default true). An endpoint upstream_defaults block replaces this wholesale.

asset_defaults.description: Global asset-serving defaults. Add-only: the block extends the gateway's built-in content-type map, it never replaces an entry in it.

content_types.description: Extension-to-Content-Type additions for extensions the gateway does not already map. ADD-ONLY: an entry naming a built-in extension (html, htm, css, js, mjs, json, map, xml, txt, svg, png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, ico, woff, woff2, ttf, pdf, wasm) is REFUSED AT BOOT, not silently ignored. The built-in mappings are immutable because remapping one — svg away from image/svg+xml, or any extension to text/html — is a stored-XSS lever on a security gateway. An extension neither map carries still falls back to application/octet-stream. The VALUE must be a well-formed type/subtype media type, optionally followed by ';name=value' parameters, and carries no control characters: it is served verbatim as the asset's Content-Type response header, so a CR/LF or non-media-type value would be a response-header-injection vector. This schema deliberately enforces only the CHEAP half of that bound — a length cap plus a flat, control-character-free 'type/subtype…' shape. The precise RFC 9110 parameter grammar is enforced at boot by the configuration validator (ConfigValidator.validateAssetContentTypeValues), which additionally names the offending extension and value. Both anchors terminate with a negative lookahead rather than '$', because the schema 'pattern' keyword is evaluated with find semantics and '$' also matches before a final line terminator — exactly the trailing CR/LF these bounds exist to refuse.

edge_hardening.description: Admission budget for the public data-plane edge. websocket_relay_cap is a sub-budget acquired in addition to the general admission permit (a relay holds its permit for the connection's whole lifetime) and must not exceed admission_cap.

allowed_egress_hosts.description: SSRF egress allowlist for 'source: http'. Omitted or empty keeps the secure default, which refuses a JWKS URL resolving to a loopback, link-local, site-local, any-local, multicast, or unique-local address. Each entry names one trusted IdP host that is exempted from that check — widen only for a trusted IdP (threat model GW-05 / BFF-07), never with a wildcard.

tls_profile.description: Name of the logical trust profile used to verify the IdP's server certificate when fetching the JWKS over 'source: http'. This names a trust profile in API Sheriff's own vocabulary; it carries no trust material and no passwords, and the deployment binds the name to concrete trust anchors. Omitted means the JVM default trust store, which is correct for an IdP presenting a publicly-trusted certificate. Name a profile when the IdP presents a certificate from an internal or corporate CA. A named profile that the deployment does not define is refused at startup — it never silently falls back to default trust.

cookie_name.description: Name of the session cookie, in both session modes; defaults to __Host-sheriff-session when omitted. The name is written verbatim into Set-Cookie, so a declared value is REFUSED AT BOOT unless it starts with the case-sensitive __Host- prefix followed by a name (the prefix is what makes the browser enforce Secure, Path=/ and no Domain), is a non-empty RFC 9110 token (no whitespace, control characters or separators such as ';' or '='), and differs from the gateway-owned cookies __Host-sheriff-binding and __Host-sheriff-logout. The rule is stated here in prose only: the configuration validator is the sole enforcing authority and names the offending value at boot, which is why no pattern keyword is declared.

max_sessions.description: Server-mode upper bound on concurrently stored sessions — a DoS guard on the in-memory store. Creating a session beyond the bound is refused fail-closed.

max_cookie_size.description: Cookie-mode sealed cookie-value size budget in bytes; valid range 40..8192, defaulting to 4019 when omitted — the browser-safe value budget, being the ~4096 bytes RFC 6265 6.1 guarantees per whole Set-Cookie header less the 77 bytes the default cookie name and attributes wrap around the value. This is the ONE declared number driving both ends of the round trip — the seal-time budget and the gateway's pre-route Cookie header-value cap — so the two can never contradict each other. The bounds are stated here in prose only: the configuration validator is the sole enforcing authority and names the offending value at boot, which is why no minimum, maximum or default keyword is declared.

user_info.description: Session/user-info reserved-endpoint settings (fold). The curated identity view the gateway serves to the browser, capped by an operator-owned claim allowlist whose secure default is closed: an empty allowed_claims discloses nothing.

allowed_claims.description: Operator claim allowlist; empty is the secure closed default that discloses nothing. The operator — never the browser client — widens disclosure.

default_view.description: Curated default-view claim selector returned when the caller requests no explicit claims; every entry must lie within allowed_claims.

login.description: Login-initiation reserved-path settings (fold). Mirrors the logout shape so the login-initiation endpoint reads as oidc.login.path.

default_return_url.description: Post-login return target used when a login carries no usable return URL: an absent, cross-origin or unparseable target falls back to it. Defaults to / when omitted. It must be same-origin with redirect_uri (a relative path, or an absolute URL on the redirect_uri origin); a cross-origin value is refused at boot (enforced in code).
